mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST YoY change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase of 0.4 percentage points or more over two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by ≥0.4pp for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing output and capacity utilization, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during non-recession periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary inflation and tightening shock, which increases risk premia and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a mixed labor market, often preceding a slowdown in wage growth and consumer confidence, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between monthly housing starts (HOUST) growth and S&P 500 5-day forward returns, reflecting sensitivity of consumer confidence and construction sector earnings to new housing activity.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST monthly growth and S&P 500 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
